subject: Latency accounting dispute: overlapping scheduled maintenance + CDN outage
messages:
From: Elaine Hsu <elaine.hsu@velocityhealth.io>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@velocityhealth.io
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 16:12:34 -0700
Subject: Latency during maintenance overlap — request for SLA accounting

Kimberly,

We observed sustained elevated p95 request latency to the /generate endpoint between 2027-05-29T20:05Z and 2027-05-29T23:22Z. Our monitoring shows two distinct causes overlapping: (a) your scheduled maintenance in eu-west-1 (2027-05-29T20:00Z - 2027-05-29T22:00Z) and (b) an unrelated FastEdge CDN outage starting ~2027-05-29T21:40Z that caused high tail latency for our users in the EU.

VelocityHealth has a 99.95% availability SLA for the generation API in our contract. We measured the impact as ~3 hours 17 minutes of degraded performance (p95 > 750ms) during that window. Per our billing team, we expect Redwood to either exclude the scheduled maintenance entirely or absorb the third-party outage and provide a credit for the portion of the time that exceeds the planned maintenance. Please provide your calculation, timeline, and proposed credit by EOD Monday.

Attached: velocity_latency_snapshot_20270529.csv (sample traces), our alert timeline.

Thanks,
Elaine Hsu\SRE, VelocityHealth

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 18:45:02 -0700
Subject: Fwd: VelocityHealth SLA dispute — overlap with FastEdge outage (need calc + recommendation)

Team — forwarding VelocityHealth's note and FastEdge timeline. Key facts we pulled from infra traces (preliminary):
- Our scheduled maintenance (eu-west-1) active window: 2027-05-29T20:00Z — 2027-05-29T22:00Z. It involved rolling kernel updates and instance restarts; we expected KV cache cold starts to affect ~12–18% of requests for ~45m total.
- Observed degradation window (client-visible p95 > 750ms): 2027-05-29T20:05Z — 2027-05-29T23:22Z (3h17m).
- FastEdge provided timeline: 21:40Z — 23:10Z (stabilized by 23:10Z, residual tail through 23:22Z).
- Overlap partition: maintenance-only: 20:05Z — 21:40Z (~1h35m); overlap: 21:40Z — 22:00Z (~20m); FastEdge-only: 22:00Z — 23:10Z (~1h10m); residual tail 23:10Z—23:22Z (~12m).

Questions for recommendations:
1) Per our SLA doc (excerpt attached as redwood-slo-excerpt.pdf), scheduled maintenance we published in advance is excluded from uptime computation only for the explicit maintenance window we notified (20:00Z–22:00Z). However, policy excludes only periods where Redwood controls the full path and has an active maintenance flag. 
2) FastEdge outage is a third-party event; the question is whether we apportion the credit or attribute it to third-party and therefore exclude it entirely from Redwood liability.

Proposed options (quick):
A) Strict policy: exclude 20:00Z–22:00Z; attribute 21:40Z–23:10Z to FastEdge -> Redwood owes no credit.
B) Customer-first: treat overlapping period (21:40Z–22:00Z) as Redwood-affecting (because our KV cold caches amplified impacts) and offer a prorated credit for overlap + the FastEdge-only period beyond our notice window (22:00Z–23:10Z) as goodwill.
C) Billing recommended: compute prorated credit for the non-excluded minutes where customer-visible p95 breached SLA, but cap at 25% of monthly invoice for goodwill.

Input requested: what does Finance and Sales think we should offer vs. what Legal would accept?

— Kimberly
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 19:30:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: VelocityHealth SLA dispute — calc proposal

Thanks Kimberly — billing did a minute-by-minute correlation against customer-observed p95 and our internal maintenance flag. Calculation summary attached (velocity_latency_snapshot_20270529.csv).

Short version:
- Total window customer flagged: 197 minutes (3h17m).
- Minutes flagged as inside published maintenance: 120 minutes (20:00Z–22:00Z). Those are contractually excluded if our maintenance flag was active; we verify it was.
- Minutes where customer-visible breach occurred outside maintenance (post-22:00Z): 77 minutes. Of those, 20 minutes (21:40Z–22:00Z) are overlap (maintenance + FastEdge outage); 57 minutes are FastEdge-only (22:00Z–23:10Z plus residual).

Policy/precedent: we typically exclude scheduled maintenance minutes from SLA calculation, but when a third-party outage worsens the impact of our cache-cold starts (i.e., our maintenance changed the baseline), we have historically offered a goodwill proration for the overlap and the third-party-only minutes beyond our scheduled window.

Proposed computation (billing):
- Apply contractual exclusion for the 120 maintenance minutes.
- Offer goodwill credit for overlap + FastEdge-only minutes: 77 minutes / (month minutes for service) * monthly invoice. That equates to ~0.17% of monthly service hours. Because customer impact was noticeable, recommend converting to a billing credit of 10% of the month's Redwood usage for VelocityHealth as a one-time goodwill (capped, per Finance).

If Sales wants to be more conciliatory, we can push to 15–20% but Finance needs approval.

— Priyom
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Hsu <elaine.hsu@velocityhealth.io>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 11:03:20 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency during maintenance overlap — proposed resolution

Elaine — thanks again for the detailed traces and patience while we investigated. Summary and proposed resolution below.

Timeline we validated: 2027-05-29T20:05Z — 2027-05-29T23:22Z (3h17m customer-visible p95 > 750ms). Our published maintenance window covered 20:00Z—22:00Z (120m) and was active in our control plane during that time. FastEdge confirmed an incident from ~21:40Z—23:10Z.

How we applied policy:
- We excluded the confirmed maintenance minutes that were within the published window (120 minutes).
- For the 77 remaining minutes where customer-visible p95 breached outside the excluded maintenance window, we attribute the root cause primarily to the FastEdge outage but acknowledge our maintenance cold-starts likely amplified customer impact during the overlap.

What we're offering:
- A one-time goodwill credit of 10% of Redwood-hosted usage on your May invoice, applied to next billing cycle. This aligns with our Finance cap and is consistent with precedent for mixed-cause events.
- We will provide the minute-by-minute correlation CSV and SLO excerpt (attached).
- Operational next steps: we will add an extra pre-warm phase to maintenance rolling restarts (reduce KV cold impact) and coordinate maintenance windows with customers who show heavy edge reliance in the future.

If you'd prefer a larger credit, we're open to negotiating up to 15% pending final sign-off from Finance — let me know.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Ops
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-slo-excerpt.pdf, velocity_latency_snapshot_20270529.csv
